title: When the Terminal Turns
premise: Sable Oyelaran has spent nine years alone tending Earth's last seed vault on the forgotten colony of Meridian's Rest, recording in her logs the quiet deaths of a settlement officially declared thriving. When a distress signal arrives in Old Vessic—a language extinct since the Kestrel Purge two centuries ago—she traces it to a buried station beneath the ice and uncovers evidence of a massacre that every official record insists never happened. As the colonial authority sends an 'audit team' to erase both the vault and its caretaker, Sable must ally with Idris, a defector archivist who helped falsify those records, to broadcast the truth before the vault's failing reactor seals it forever. She succeeds at terrible cost: the truth escapes, but Sable chooses to stay behind with the dying vault, becoming the archive herself—her voice joining the signal that once saved her.
about_author: O. M. Hartwell is a former agricultural scientist who spent a decade cataloguing heirloom seeds before turning to fiction about what survives us. They write from a converted greenhouse on the northern coast, where they keep a living archive of plants most of the world has forgotten how to grow.

chapters.title: The Last Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Establishes her solitary routine: logging germination rates, rationing power, speaking aloud to seedlings because silence is worse. Emotional beat: tender loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Census of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sable reviews colony records showing Meridian's Rest listed as 40,000 strong; she counts eleven survivors including herself. POV Sable. Beat: quiet outrage hardening into purpose—her logs are testimony.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: The vault's ancient receiver catches a repeating burst in Old Vessic. Sable, whose grandmother sang lullabies in it, recognizes it instantly. Beat: wonder cracking through isolation—the first contact in years.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Sang
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Sable's POV, to childhood lessons in Old Vessic and why the language was purged after the Kestrel Rebellion. Beat: grief for erased heritage; she begins translating.

chapters.title: Beneath the Ice Shelf
chapters.summary: Sable triangulates the signal to Station Kestrel-9 under the glacier. She must leave the vault for the first time in three years. Beat: fear of abandonment versus compulsion to know.

chapters.title: The Door That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable breaches the station's outer lock, finding scorch marks and a sealed blast door scratched from the inside. Beat: dread mounting—the scratches are handprints, hundreds.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Airlock
chapters.summary: Inside, she finds preserved bodies and a data core still cycling the distress call. POV Sable. Beat: horror transmuting into resolve—someone wanted this found.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Idris Vane arrives unannounced at the vault, claiming to be a supply auditor but carrying forbidden Kestrel-era documents. His POV opens the dual structure. Beat: wary mutual recognition of liars.

chapters.title: Two Liars at Dinner
chapters.summary: Sable conceals the station discovery; Idris conceals his real orders. Over reconstituted stew they probe each other. Beat: electric tension, first flicker of attraction through deception.

chapters.title: Records That Lie
chapters.summary: Idris privately confirms the official history was fabricated by the Colonial Authority after the massacre. His guilt drives him. Beat: shame—he wrote some of the lies himself.

chapters.title: Translation
chapters.summary: Sable finally decodes the distress message: not a plea for rescue but a warning—'they will say we never were.' Beat: devastating clarity; the dead predicted their own erasure.

chapters.title: The Audit Team
chapters.summary: Authority transmission: an audit vessel inbound in forty days to 'decommission' the vault. Idris reveals his cover is real—he was sent ahead. Beat: betrayal and reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Terms of Trust
chapters.summary: Sable and Idris negotiate: he'll help broadcast the evidence if she lets him destroy the data core that names him. Beat: love against duty begins—neither fully trusts, both need.

chapters.title: Reactor Mathematics
chapters.summary: Hard-SF interlude: the vault's reactor will fail within months regardless; broadcasting requires diverting its remaining power. Beat: cold arithmetic framing the price of survival.

chapters.title: Names of the Dead
chapters.summary: Sable catalogs the station victims, restoring identities the records deleted. Beat: mourning as resistance; each name spoken aloud in Old Vessic.

chapters.title: Idris's Confession
chapters.summary: Idris admits he authored the erasure protocols as a young archivist believing order required mercy-lies. Beat: self-loathing met by Sable's unexpected grace.

chapters.title: First Kiss, Last Argument
chapters.summary: After a near-fatal crevasse crossing, intimacy breaks open between them—and immediately collides with their conflicting missions. Beat: tenderness shadowed by inevitability.

chapters.title: The Authority's Ear
chapters.summary: They discover the audit ship can monitor surface transmissions; any broadcast attempt will be traced and jammed. Beat: the plan needs a miracle or a sacrifice.

chapters.title: Relay of the Rebels
chapters.summary: A derelict orbital relay from the Kestrel era might still function—if someone reaches it physically. Beat: hope with a body count attached.

chapters.title: Preparations
chapters.summary: Quiet domestic chapter: repairing a land crawler, planting one last bed of seeds, dancing badly to salvaged music. Beat: stolen happiness, deliberately savored.

chapters.title: The Choice of Seeds
chapters.summary: Sable must decide which seed stocks to load as ballast-proof cargo if evacuation becomes possible. Beat: the curator's dilemma—what deserves to outlive her.

chapters.title: Audit Ship Arrival
chapters.summary: The vessel descends early; Auditor Chen broadcasts a courteous demand for surrender of all archives. Beat: menace wrapped in bureaucracy.

chapters.title: Chen's Offer
chapters.summary: Chen privately offers Sable extraction and a new identity if she surrenders the core. Beat: temptation—survival offered at the exact price of meaning.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Sable declines, quoting the distress message back to Chen, who flinches—she knows the truth too. Beat: courage crystallizing; the mask slips on both sides.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Audit teams begin stripping the vault; Idris secretly corrupts their downloads while Sable plays cooperative caretaker. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension, escalating stakes.

chapters.title: Caught
chapters.summary: Idris is discovered mid-sabotage and detained. Sable watches via hidden camera, unable to intervene. Beat: gut-punch helplessness; love tested by duty's cost.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Idris's POV under questioning; he protects Sable by claiming sole responsibility. Beat: sacrifice as atonement—he finally lies for the truth.

chapters.title: Alone Again, Differently
chapters.summary: Sable, now hunted, prepares the crawler alone, keeping Idris alive in her head as dialogue. Beat: loneliness transformed—she was never really alone again.

chapters.title: The Reactor Gambit
chapters.summary: She reroutes the vault's dying reactor to charge the relay's launch beacon, knowing it dooms the vault's climate systems. Beat: irrevocable choice; the price named.

chapters.title: Ice Run
chapters.summary: Driving sequence across the glacier pursued by audit skimmers, using storm cover. Beat: kinetic terror and exhilaration—freedom at full throttle.

chapters.title: Kestrel-9 Revisited
chapters.summary: Sable retrieves the data core from the station, speaking the victims' names over the bodies as farewell. Beat: communion with the dead; mission sanctified.

chapters.title: The Relay Climb
chapters.summary: Orbital elevator fragment climb to the derelict relay, oxygen failing. Beat: vertigo and determination—her body as the last cable of truth.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Sable transmits the massacre evidence, the original distress signal, and her own logs to every colony band. Beat: triumphant catharsis cut short by alarms.

chapters.title: Jamming
chapters.summary: The audit ship jams the relay; only a fraction escaped. Chen offers terms again: silence for Idris's life. Beat: cruel dilemma—truth incomplete, love held hostage.

chapters.title: What Survives
chapters.summary: Sable realizes the escaped fragment already seeded independent networks; the erasure is impossible now. She refuses the trade. Beat: faith over leverage.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Vault
chapters.summary: Chen comes for her personally; Sable triggers the vault's final protocol—sealing the seeds in cryo-archive and locking them both inside as the reactor dies. Beat: climax; witness made literal.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Archive
chapters.summary: Trapped, Sable records her final testimony; Chen, confronted with the dying woman's calm, breaks and releases the vault seal, choosing conscience. Beat: antagonist's redemption, ambiguous and earned.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Rescue ships arrive responding to the broadcast; Idris freed, testifies publicly. The galaxy learns of Meridian's Rest. Beat: vindication hollowed by absence.

chapters.title: Seeds in New Ground
chapters.summary: Epilogue: colonists reopen the vault years later, finding Sable's logs and a single sprouted seed she planted before the end. Beat: bittersweet continuity—she became part of the archive.

chapters.title: When the Terminal Turns
chapters.summary: Final chapter: Idris, now keeper of the restored vault, receives a faint repeating signal in Old Vessic—Sable's log voice woven into the old distress call, still teaching. Beat: transcendent closure; love outlasting duty, death, and silence.
